Furthermore, factors such as slight registration errors and local textural noise often trigger high-frequency pseudo-change responses, leading to false detections. To this end, this article proposes a lightweight dual-domain directional network (LDDN) for resource-constrained scenarios, achieving efficient and reliable change detection through the synergistic design of frequency-domain noise suppression and spatial-domain directional modeling. Specifically, to suppress unreliable high-frequency responses induced by factors like registration errors, a directional wavelet attention module (DWAM) is designed. It utilizes the directional high-frequency subbands of the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to perform adaptive screening, thereby suppressing unreliable components and mining structural cues associated with real changes. To enhance the capability of lightweight models in capturing weak change targets, a directional spatial fusion module (DSFM) is proposed, which constructs long-range anisotropic modeling capabilities at a low cost by decoupling horizontal and vertical contextual dependencies. Furthermore, to ensure semantic consistency across multiple scales, a multiscale interaction module (MIM) is introduced to facilitate cross-scale synergy between frequency-domain filtering and spatial-domain directional modeling. The experimental results demonstrate that with only 1.98M parameters and 2.58G FLOPs, LDDN achieves competitive or superior detection performance compared to various state-of-the-art methods across four public benchmark datasets. Particularly on the challenging CLCD dataset, the  $F1$ -score and intersection over union (IoU) are improved by 0.83% and 1.07%, respectively, compared to the second-best method. The code is available at: https://github.com/Vi-chen/LDDN
author: Wei Wang, Shengli Chen, Xin Wang, Xingwei Zhu

title: Interfacial-Crack-State Assessment Using Effective Dielectric Characteristics With EM-Wave Responses
content: Interfacial microcracks can compromise the sealing and barrier performance of subsurface energy systems, yet their dielectric observability and electromagnetic wavefield expression remain insufficiently quantified under roughness, local contact, fluid infill, and background heterogeneity. Here, we establish an integrated experimental–numerical framework for cracked bilayer interfaces by combining waveguide-based microwave measurements, representative elementary volume (REV)-scale dielectric homogenization, analytical mixing-law benchmarking, and 6-GHz finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) wavefield simulations. Waveguide measurements over 5.35–8.17 GHz demonstrate that intact interfaces, air-filled cracks, and water-filled cracks can be distinguished through S-parameters, retrieved effective permittivity, and reflection–transmission–absorption energy partitioning. Numerical homogenization shows that crack inclination and volume fraction primarily control the real effective permittivity, roughness and spatial position modulate dielectric contrast through field redistribution, and salinity is more clearly expressed through effective conductivity. Benchmarking against Bruggeman–Hanai–Sen (BHS), complex refractive index model (CRIM), and Lorentz–Lorenz/Clausius–Mossotti (LLCM) indicates that phase-fraction-based mixing laws may substantially overestimate the contribution of high-permittivity crack fillings when rough-surface mismatch and local solid-to-solid contact are present, whereas a calibrated BHS model with c = 0.75 gives the closest approximation within the examined range. FDTD simulations further show that crack-induced dielectric contrasts generate observable reflection–diffraction characteristics in A-scan, B-scan, and spectral responses. Reference-based residual-wavefield descriptors reveal that crack state mainly reorganizes spatial and spectral energy distributions rather than producing simple monotonic amplitude enhancement. These findings provide a physically constrained basis for interpreting interfacial microcrack states in high-frequency GPR-based nondestructive assessment of bilayer systems.
author: Xinhao Yu, Diansen Yang, Weiming Liang, Yuna Cai, Junwei Xu

title: Efficient Spatio-Temporal Processing for Multichannel Radar Forward-Looking Imaging
content: By simultaneously exploiting the time-domain and space-domain resources of the echoes from multiple channels in the azimuth direction, multichannel radar can achieve ambiguity-free forward-looking imaging. However, the along-flight path area suffers from poor imaging performance due to small Doppler variation. Although superresolution can enhance imaging performance, they always face the problem of azimuthal spatial variation of the point spread function (PSF) and heavy computational burden caused by a large-scale echo matrix. To address these issues, an efficient spatio-temporal imaging scheme is proposed in this article. First, according to the azimuth-variant law of the PSF, the echoes from the along-track region and the off-track region are separated by making use of the Doppler differences in different regions. Then, the spatio-temporal steering matrices for different echoes are constructed, and the imaging is achieved by using the superresolution and the spatio-temporal beamforming processing, respectively. Finally, the two results are combined to obtain the final imaging result. Simulations and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly reduces computational burden and indirectly overcomes the problem of spatial variation of PSFs, thus achieving better superresolution performance.
author: Rui Chen, Wenchao Li, Jianyu Yang, Bowen Cheng, Kun Zhang, Junjie Wu

title: DMGNN: Diffusion-Enhanced Multimodal Graph Neural Network for HSI and LiDAR Classification
content: The fusion of hyperspectral images (HSIs) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data has become a cornerstone in remote sensing classification, leveraging complementary spectral and elevation information for accurate land cover classification. However, when modeling complex spatial relationships under limited labeled samples, the existing graph-based approaches often suffer from a “broken topology,” i.e., a sparse and fragmented network structure that severely limits information flow. To address this limitation, in this work, we propose a novel diffusion-enhanced multimodal graph neural network (DMGNN), which takes the inherent topological advantages of graph representations to effectively model complex multimodal structures. A diffusion-enhanced multimodal graph construction module is first formulated to generate synthetic nodes that densify the fragmented topology, ensuring effective message passing even in sparse data regions. Second, a spectral clustering-guided pretraining strategy is introduced to mine the global cluster structure of the multimodal graph for superior parameter initialization. Third, a dynamic multimodal contrastive learning mechanism is constructed to enforce structural robustness and cross-modal alignment within the node embeddings. Fourth, an adaptive feature extraction and multiobjective optimization module is introduced to refine multiscale features and handle class imbalance. By flexibly utilizing topological structures, our method successfully addresses the scarcity of effective graph-based approaches. Extensive experiments on three widely used HSI and LiDAR datasets demonstrate that our proposed DMGNN outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our method achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 99.88% on Houston2013, 99.50% on Trento, and 95.14% on highly imbalanced Houston2018_sliced dataset. The codebase is now publicly available at https://github.com/11451419198106324/DMGNN
author: Changda Xing, Yifang Wu, Yongchang Xu, Cheng Wang, Meiling Wang

title: Vision-Language Model Purified Semisupervised Semantic Segmentation for Remote Sensing Images
content: The semisupervised semantic segmentation (S4) can learn rich visual knowledge from low-cost, unlabeled images. However, traditional S4 architectures all face the challenge of low-quality pseudolabels, especially in the teacher–student framework. We propose a novel SemiEarth model that introduces vision-language models (VLMs) to address the S4 issues in the remote sensing (RS) domain. In particular, we invent a VLM pseudolabel purifying (VLM-PP) structure to purify the teacher network’s pseudolabels, achieving substantial improvements. Especially in multiclass boundary regions of RS images, the VLM-PP module can significantly improve the quality of pseudolabels generated by the teacher, thereby correctly guiding the student model’s learning. Moreover, since VLM-PP equips VLMs with open-world capabilities and is independent of the S4 architecture, it can correct mispredicted categories in low-confidence pseudolabels whenever a discrepancy arises between its prediction and the pseudolabel. We conducted extensive experiments on multiple RS datasets, which demonstrate that our semiEarth achieves SOTA performance. More importantly, unlike previous SOTA RS S4 methods, our model not only achieves excellent performance but also offers good interpretability. The code is released at https://github.com/wangshanwen001/SemiEarth
author: Shanwen Wang, Xin Sun, Danfeng Hong, Fei Zhou

title: TFVP-MLLM: Training-Free Visual Prompting Multimodal Large Language Model for Remote Sensing Image Classification
content: The multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved breakthroughs in remote sensing applications because of their powerful cross-modal understanding, enabling effective alignment between linguistic descriptions and visual data. However, the existing MLLM-based approaches still suffer from challenges, such as inaccurate region localization, limited domain adaptability, and high computational costs. To overcome these limitations, we propose a training-free visual prompting MLLM called TFVP-MLLM, which is built on visual prompting guidance and a scoring feedback mechanism to achieve high-quality remote sensing image classification under low resource constraints. Our TFVP-MLLM is composed of the category proposal generator (CPG) and the score feedback refiner (SFR). The CPG is responsible for generating high-quality candidate categories by integrating the proposed geographic priors injection module (GPIM) and hybrid-granularity region attention loss (HGRAL). Meanwhile, SFR uses an iterative generate and score process to enhance the accuracy and reliability of the candidate categories. As two critical components of CPG, GPIM incorporates prior geographic knowledge to significantly improve the model’s domain adaptation, while HGRAL optimizes visual token representations with several frozen modules to reduce computational requirements. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed TFVP-MLLM, the comprehensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets UCM, AID, and DIOR-RSVG. For the scene classification task, TFVP-MLLM achieves the state-of-the-art performance among training-free multimodal approaches with overall classification accuracies of 97.8% and 82.4% on the UCM and AID datasets, respectively. For the regional object classification task, TFVP-MLLM achieves remarkable scores of 92.4% semantic similarity (SS) and 88.6% semantic intersection over union (SIOU) on the DIOR-RSVG dataset, which surpasses the other training-free methods and even achieves comparable results against supervised approaches. In addition, we perform a series of ablation studies to confirm the effectiveness of each module. The source code is available at https://github.com/Camellia86/TFVP-MLLM
author: Yifei Xu, Zixiang Ni, Pingping Wei, Chufan Xiao, Yaochen Li, Agen Qiu, Dong Li, Yuan Rao

title: Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation is vital for remote sensing applications, where accurate feature extraction and representation are essential. Existing encoder–decoder architectures often fail to fully utilize high-dimensional features and recover fine details during decoding. To address this problem, we propose DeepKANSeg, a novel network based on the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN). KAN’s ability to decompose complex functions into univariate transformations enables flexible modeling of intricate data patterns. Our approach introduces two key innovations: a KAN-based deep feature refinement (DFR) module composed of DeepKAN to capture complex spatial and semantic relationships from high-dimensional features, and a global–local KAN (GLKAN) module replacing the traditional multilayer perceptron (MLP) layers with KAN-based linear layers to enhance fine-grained decoding. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, extensive experiments are conducted on two well-known fine-resolution remote sensing benchmark datasets, namely ISPRS Vaihingen and ISPRS Potsdam. The results demonstrate that the KAN-enhanced segmentation model achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the univariate decomposition improves interpretability, making it suitable for explainable learning in remote sensing. The source code for this work will be accessible at https://github.com/sstary/SSRS
author: Ziyao Wang, Yin Hu, Xiaokang Zhang, Yuanxin Ye, Xianping Ma, Man-On Pun

title: A Unified On-Orbit Relative Radiometric Calibration Framework for Optical Remote Sensing Satellites Based on Side-Slither Observations
content: On-orbit relative radiometric calibration (RRC) is a fundamental prerequisite for quantitative remote sensing analysis and high-level product generation. Although side-slither maneuvers provide a robust means for calibration, existing methodologies are often constrained by regularization inaccuracies, uneven distribution of gray-scale samples, and limited adaptability to complex multisensor architectures. This article proposes a unified RRC framework to overcome these challenges. The process begins with a prior-guided optimization method for data regularization, which operates independently of linear features or edges. To handle the inherently uneven distribution of gray-scale samples across natural scenes, an adaptive clustering-based method is implemented to estimate calibration coefficients. This approach ensures stable performance across the observed effective dynamic range, particularly in gray-scale ranges where samples are sparse. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a detail-aware strategy to achieve high-precision calibration across the full field of view (FOV). Specifically, the virtual steady reimaging (VSRI) model is first leveraged to achieve rigorous spatial alignment of identical ground features across multiple sensors. Based on this precise geometric alignment, the radiometric calibration is subsequently anchored to an optimal reference radiometric state. This approach effectively eliminates cross-chip inconsistencies while preserving structural details. Validation using side-slither and push-broom data from the Intelligent Remote Sensing Satellite-1 (IRSS-1), Luojia3-02 (LJ3-02), and Ziyuan-1F (ZY-1F) satellites demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed approach across diverse scenes, sensor architectures, and spectral bands. Comparative analyses show that the proposed method achieves overall superior performance over four state-of-the-art methods in removing striping artifacts and maintaining radiometric fidelity.
author: Tao Peng, Ru Chen, Qianyu Wu, Tingjian Yang, Qiongqiong Lan, Mi Wang

title: DPCDO: Dynamic-Coordinated Learning for Multitask Domain Adaptation in Remote Sensing Imagery
content: Unified architectures that jointly perform semantic segmentation and monocular height estimation offer improved computational efficiency through shared representations, but face challenges in remote sensing applications: scarce annotations, intertask interference, and cross-regional domain shifts. These issues often lead to severe performance degradation, as models struggle with domain discrepancies and conflicting gradients. Moreover, existing domain adaptation methods remain constrained, suffering from low pseudolabel confidence, feature misalignment, and negative transfer. To address these, we propose DPCDO, a dynamic-coordinated learning approach for unsupervised multitask domain adaptation, which jointly models the multivariate conditional generation process of task outputs, domain alignment, and pseudolabel consistency. DPCDO integrates three synergistic modules: 1) dynamic patchwise prototype matching dynamically aligns local feature distributions to accommodate topographic diversity, promoting domain-invariant representation learning and cross-task information sharing; 2) multistream multiscale consistency constraint performs multiscale perturbations and enforces cross-stream consistency to enhance pseudolabel reliability; and 3) decoupled optimization for multitask heads to resolve intertask gradient conflicts. Extensive experiments show DPCDO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both semantic segmentation and monocular height estimation, validating its effectiveness in disentangling domain shifts and enhancing cross-task synergy.
author: Zitong Wu, Yaoyao Yin, Biao Hou, Bo Ren, Xianpeng Guo, Zhengxi Guo

title: Spatial–Temporal Collaborative Network for Satellite Image Time Series Semantic Change Detection
content: Semantic change detection (SCD) aims to generate both semantic segmentation maps and binary change (BC) maps from binary temporal remote sensing images and plays a crucial role in remote sensing image interpretation. While learning-based methods have shown strong performance on standard benchmarks, the more challenging satellite image time series (SITS)-based SCD task remains underexplored. Existing SITS-SCD approaches often overemphasize temporal cues while neglecting effective spatial–temporal interaction and are stuck in low-efficiency feature fusion, limiting their representation capacity. To this end, we propose ST3DUNet, a spatial–temporal collaborative network for SITS-SCD. ST3DUNet adopts a U-shaped architecture that extracts hierarchical spatial–temporal representations through a bidirectional spatial–temporal module (BSTM) and recursively fuses them via a collaborative fusion block (CFB) based on dynamically updated prototype matrices. This collaborative fusion enhances decoding by leveraging informative spatial–temporal embeddings. Moreover, we evaluate the robustness of our model under spatial domain shifts, which adhere to real-world remote sensing image decryption conditions. Extensive experiments on three SITS datasets demonstrate that ST3DUNet consistently outperforms independent temporal processing, pairwise temporal modeling, and existing SITS-SCD methods, as well as three Earth observation foundation models (FMs), achieving consistent improvements of approximately +5%, +3%, and +5% in mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) across DynamicEarthNet-RGB, DynamicEarthNet-Sentinel2, and Muds, respectively. Code will be released at https://github.com/xuwayyy/ST3DUNet
author: Jiangwei Xie, Yuxiang Zhang, Mengmeng Zhang, Yan Du, Wei Li

title: GLoP-SAM3: A Dual Postprocessing Framework With Global–Local Prior Fusion and Reliability Gating for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
content: Open-vocabulary remote sensing semantic segmentation enables pixel-level recognition of arbitrary semantic categories through text prompts, providing an effective way to reduce the dependence of traditional closed-set remote sensing segmentation on fixed category sets and large-scale annotations. However, existing training-free methods in remote sensing scenarios still mainly rely on local responses and sliding-window inference and thus suffer from insufficient utilization of full-image global semantic priors, unstable local predictions, and unreliable prior propagation. To address these issues, we propose GLoP-SAM3, a dual postprocessing framework for open-vocabulary remote sensing semantic segmentation, whose core idea is to enhance performance through two lightweight postprocessing modules rather than introducing a new backbone or complex trainable components. Specifically, we develop a divergence-aware global–local fusion (DGLF) module, which adaptively integrates full-image semantic priors with local predictions by jointly modeling local–global discrepancy and local confidence, and a reliability-gated prediction refinement (RGPR) module, which suppresses erroneous prior propagation and improves segmentation quality in complex and boundary regions through high-confidence preservation, ambiguous-region enhancement, and prior reliability gating. Built upon SAM3 without any additional training, the proposed method introduces only limited computational overhead while significantly improving prediction consistency and segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on eight public remote sensing datasets demonstrate that GLoP-SAM3 consistently improves the baseline and achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance under the training-free setting on representative benchmarks such as OpenEarthMap, validating the favorable balance of the proposed dual postprocessing strategy between efficiency and performance. The code, fixed prompts, and configuration files are available at https://github.com/LiorCohen0901/GLoP-SAM
author: Chang Liu, Yuzhuo Han, Xiangzhe Kong, Mingjie Li, Yonghua Li

title: Efficient PS Wavefield Separation for Anisotropic VTI and TTI Media in the Spatial Domain
content: Compared with conventional P-wave exploration technology, multiwave and multicomponent seismic exploration technology can more accurately characterize subsurface geological structures and delineate hydrocarbon reservoir features. During the propagation of seismic waves in real strata, coupled P-wave and S-wave fields generate imaging crosstalk noise, significantly degrading the quality of imaging profiles. Consequently, the critical challenge in multicomponent exploration lies in P/S wave decoupling prior to imaging. Current conventional wavefield decomposition methods, which require extensive Fourier and inverse Fourier transforms, often suffer from high computational and separation costs due to inefficient decoupling in practical applications. This article proposed a novel P-/S-wave decoupling method that operates entirely in the spatial domain, eliminating the need for Fourier and inverse Fourier transforms while maintaining effective separation. In the numerical experiments for vertical transverse isotropic (VTI) media, a homogeneous anisotropic velocity model, a horizontal layered anisotropic VTI model, and the complex Hess VTI model are used. To further demonstrate model generality, we also test the P/S wavefield separation performance in TTI media using homogeneous and layered anisotropic models. In all numerical examples, the proposed method delivers consistently high-quality P/S separation, with strong crosstalk suppression and stable performance in the presence of lateral heterogeneity, confirming its suitability for a broad range of anisotropic scenarios. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method maintains low crosstalk leakage and achieves approximately 5–6 times higher computational efficiency than conventional methods while preserving separation accuracy.
author: Qingyou Zhi, Jiachun You, Yiyang Jiang, Haipeng Hu

title: Interferometric Phase Map Segmentation Algorithm Based on an Adaptive Optimization Tolerance Granularity Space Model
content: In large-scale and complex environments, phase unwrapping using a unified method over the entire interferometric phase map (IPM) of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) often suffers from error propagation, where noise in low-quality regions spreads across the IPM and degrades the overall unwrapping accuracy. To address this issue, segmenting IPMs based on phase quality and noise distribution, followed by region-specific processing, is a reasonable and feasible strategy. An IPM segmentation algorithm based on adaptively optimized tolerance granular space model (TGSM) is proposed. The IPMs are first uniformly divided into subblocks, each treated as an original object of TGSM. Five-dimensional features, including amplitude variance of interferogram and phase gradient standard deviation, among others, are used for segmentation. A weighted squared Euclidean distance is introduced serves as the similarity measure within the tolerance relation, and recursive merging of tolerance granules is controlled by searching for an optimal similarity measure threshold. In this way, a coarse-to-fine multilevel TGSM is constructed to partition complex InSAR IPMs into multiple regions. To enhance performance, an adaptive genetic algorithm is used to determine feature weights; an adaptive similarity measure threshold searching and threshold interval boundary extension strategy is adopted to improve merging reliability; small subregion merging is employed to avoid postunwrapping stitching errors that may outweigh the benefits of preunwrapping segmentation. Experiments with Sentinel-1A data show that the proposed algorithm can effectively segments the varying quality regions of IPMs. Its results outperform the other three comparison methods on all four used evaluation metrics.
author: Yifan Feng, Zhaoxia Wang, Linglin Wang, Yongsheng Qi

title: DACE-Net: Detail-Aware Calibrated Enhancement Network for Building Change Detection
content: As one of the critical tasks in urban change interpretation, building change detection aims to acquire large-scale spatial distribution change information of buildings in high-resolution remote sensing images. The false detection of pseudochanges remains a significant challenge impacting detection accuracy. Remote sensing building images exhibit complex and diverse regular texture details and boundary features. However, current change detection methods suffer from two limitations. First, an insufficient capability in extracting long-range texture features during the feature extraction stage, and second, limited effectiveness of existing detail enhancement methods in optimizing detail features during the feature restoration stage. To address these challenges, this article proposes a detail-aware calibrated enhancement network (DACE-Net). The DACE-Net employs a Siamese encoder constructed with VMamba encoder blocks for feature extraction and long-range regular texture feature modeling. It further collaborates with subsequent explicit detail calibration and implicit enhancement to refine the detail information in fused features. The synergistic approach enables comprehensive feature enhancement and effectively suppresses the representation of pseudochanges. Extensive experiments on four widely used datasets demonstrate DACE-Net’s superior performance, achieving state-of-the-art F1/intersection over union scores of 86.06%/75.52%, 91.50%/84.33%, 92.53%/86.09%, and 85.15%/74.14% on the LEVIR-CD+, LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and EGY-BCD datasets, respectively. These results outperform the current state-of-the-art methods, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed DACE-Net. The code is available online.
author: Fenglei Chen, Xiaoheng Tan, Zhihong Zeng, Hailin Cao, Haijun Liu

title: CPAZMaL: A New Dataset of X-Band SAR Time Series in the French Alps for Machine Learning
content: High-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series datasets remain scarce for high-mountain land cover applications, limiting the development of advanced machine learning methods for temporal monitoring of mountain surfaces in complex Alpine terrain. This article introduces Cryosphere analysis with PAZ images for Machine Learning, a comprehensive benchmark dataset combining three years of X-band SAR acquisitions from PAZ satellites over the Mont-Blanc massif (Western European Alps). The dataset encompasses eight terrain classes, including rarely studied glacier types, such as ice aprons and hanging glaciers alongside well-characterized accumulation and ablation zones, as well as nonglacial surfaces, such as rock outcrops, Alpine grasslands, and forested areas, enabling the study of landscape transitions driven by climate change. All the SAR images were processed through a standardized radiometric calibration and terrain correction workflow using a custom 1.5-m LiDAR DEM, ensuring geometric and radiometric consistency across dual-polarization (HH/HV) and both orbit (ascending/descending) configurations. Data are organized in a hierarchical HDF5 structure with group-based sampling to minimize spatial autocorrelation. We establish baseline performance across four machine learning scenarios: temporal classification, time-series forecasting, domain adaptation, and addressing polarimetric and cross-sensor transfer. Results demonstrate the dataset's utility for developing robust classification methods that handle geometric distortions, temporal variability, and the limited training samples inherent to high-resolution SAR data in steep Alpine environments, with a strong emphasis on glacial dynamics.
author: Matthieu Gallet, Suvrat Kaushik, Christophe Lin-Kwong-Chon, Ludovic Ravanel, Emmanuel Trouvé

title: Frequency-Aware Prompt Learning for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
content: Remote sensing image super-resolution is a critical task for reconstructing high-fidelity images from low-resolution observations. However, practical remote sensing scenarios often involve complex, compound degradations that severely compromise essential high-frequency structures, such as sharp edges and fine textures. While conventional convolutional neural network and Transformer-based methods have shown promise, they predominantly rely on static feature representations that lack adaptability to diverse scenes and often struggle to restore specific high-frequency details due to spectral bias. To this end, we propose a novel frequency-aware prompt learning framework. Specifically, a frequency-aware transformer module is designed to leverage the fast Fourier transform for explicit high-frequency component restoration, thereby overcoming the frequency bias inherent in spatial-domain models and effectively recovering intricate structural details. Concurrently, a dynamically generated prompt modulator is introduced to provide scene-specific adaptability via learnable vectors. This allows the network to adaptively calibrate feature responses to mitigate diverse environmental variations and compound artifacts. This synergistic integration ensures superior reconstruction fidelity and robust generalization across heterogeneous remote sensing scenarios. Comprehensive experiments across three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves outstanding performance in both quantitative metrics and visual quality assessments.
author: Kangli Zeng, Hang Hu, Ying Yu, Jiaming Wang, Wenhui Dong, Jie You, Hui Wang, Yu Wang

title: Fourier-Calibrated Dynamic Prompts for Universal Hyperspectral Image Restoration
content: Universal hyperspectral image (HSI) restoration aims to handle diverse and unknown degradations using a single unified model. Currently, researchers often use textual descriptions to generate prompts to guide the process. However, while such textual prompts provide high-level semantic cues, these driven prompts are typically fixed and struggle to perceive continuous physical variations in degradation intensity, which limits restoration accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a novel fourier-calibrated dynamic prompts hyperspectral image restoration (FCDP-HSIR) framework for universal HSI restoration. Unlike static designs, our method combines spatial statistics and energy characteristics in the frequency domain to better describe degradation patterns. First, the model identifies degradation categories by matching joint spatial and frequency features to predefined prototypes. A conditional Gaussian mixture distribution is then used to model intensity changes, allowing the network to sample instance-aware dynamic prompts that match the real corruption severity. Furthermore, a structure-prior spectral attention module is introduced to enhance feature reconstruction. By utilizing spatial priors to guide spectral recovery, this module effectively maintains spectral fidelity and preserves fine geometric structures. Extensive experiments across seven tasks show that FCDP-HSIR outperforms existing universal methods on most tasks and achieves competitive performance comparable to task-specific models in several representative scenarios.
author: Wenqing Shan, Zhehui Wu, Xi-Le Zhao, Wei He, Yong Chen

title: CarbonCLIP: Enhance Carbon Prediction From Satellite Imagery via Integrated Street-View Semantics and Temporal Context Training
content: Accurately estimating urban carbon emissions is critical for sustainable urban planning, yet many existing approaches remain difficult to apply consistently across cities due to data-source heterogeneity and the lack of fine-grained semantic-temporal context in remote sensing data. We propose CarbonCLIP, a task-oriented multimodal distillation framework that improves satellite-based carbon emission prediction by transferring contextual knowledge into a unified satellite representation through dual-branch contrastive learning. Unlike conventional methods that rely on static visual features, CarbonCLIP explicitly bridges the gap between top-down satellite views and ground-level human activities. Specifically, the spatial branch uses fine-grained textual descriptions automatically generated from street-view images by Large Multimodal Models to provide semantic priors reflecting building functions, infrastructure, and urban activities, while the temporal branch employs a month encoder to encode temporal priors associated with monthly emission variation. CarbonCLIP requires multimodal data only during the pretraining phase; during inference, it relies solely on satellite imagery, thereby supporting scalable deployment when ground-level data are unavailable at inference. Experiments on Beijing and Singapore demonstrate that CarbonCLIP outperforms baselines in both study cities. The results validate that our method effectively transfers multimodal knowledge into satellite representations, offering a robust solution for satellite-based urban carbon modeling.
author: Zeru Yang, Fang-Ying Gong, Steve H. L. Yim, Chau Yuen

title: A Hybrid Approach Using Statistics and Unsupervised Learning to Investigate the Impact of Ionospheric Storm Disturbances on Pre-Earthquake Total Electron Content Anomalies
content: The identification of ionospheric total electron content (TEC) anomalies as potential earthquake precursors is complicated by strong background variability driven by geomagnetic disturbances and by the spatial dispersion inherent in traditional statistical testing. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid framework that integrates one-proportion z-test statistical validation with unsupervised k-means clustering and incorporates a spatial anomaly verification stage to extract physically meaningful temporal–polarity features from global ionosphere map TEC data. The framework was first applied on 21 June 2022 ${{M}_w}$ 6.0 Afghanistan earthquake, a case preceded by a moderate geomagnetic storm within the 30-day analysis window. A negative anomaly cluster centered on Day 22 emerged as the only feature that passed both statistical- and spatial-consistency tests, with epicentral enhancement occurring during the storm recovery phase, suggesting constructive interference between storm-time ionospheric dynamics and seismogenic processes. To evaluate cross-regional robustness, the framework was further tested on 11 March 2011 ${{M}_w}$ 9.1 Tohoku earthquake, yielding a similarly isolated and spatially validated precursor feature despite substantial differences in tectonic setting, magnitude, and space weather conditions. These results demonstrate the transferability of the proposed methodology across diverse environments. The extracted features offer structured, physically informed inputs that may support future development of data-driven earthquake monitoring and early warning systems.
